analysis: The PR changes only documentation: docs/architecture/inference.md (new prompt-chunk attention row at head line 671) and docs/reference/configuration.md (date bump at line 3, new DARKBLOOM_TTFT_FUSED_CAUSAL_PREFILL row near line 313). No source, protocol, authorization, attestation, key-handling, or cache-storage code is modified. The documented behavior is a performance change: full-attention prompt chunks with MLX-fused head geometry take one .causal SDPA call instead of 128-query blocks, with live packed paged KV excluded. The kill switch is exact `0`, read once per process and not forwarded to LaunchAgents. I traced this against the threat model: A-001 and TB-007 (T-028, T-041) are the nearest. The change alters attention compute scheduling and does not touch prefix-cache identity, HMAC lookup tags, TTL, salts, or at-rest crypto. A possible TTFT timing shift is not a new cross-tenant channel beyond the accepted SEC-035 oracle. Each added env knob is local to the process and cannot be set by consumers or the coordinator, so it adds no new trust-boundary input. The large unit blocks (inference.md lines 801-1587) are unchanged surrounding text, with no changed range outside line 671. Unverified: the actual AttentionV1.swift implementation and any numerical or memory-bound effects of the single fused call (a score tensor sized by chunk length could affect memory-admission assumptions) are outside the supplied evidence. The next pass should check that code if it is in the PR. No security regression is identified from the documentation alone.
